 California’s New Reality: First In A Series From Chuck Michel
 November 17, 2026 
 CRPA 
 Legislation 
 Litigation 
 Dear CRPA Members and Supporters,
 California is preparing for a new legislative session under significantly changed political circumstances.
 Xavier Becerra has been elected Governor, Rob Bonta has won another term as Attorney General, and Democrats have expanded their already substantial legislative majorities. Although final certification is pending, the results reported so far establish Democratic supermajorities in both houses.
 Those majorities matter. Ordinary legislation generally requires 41 votes in the Assembly and 21 in the Senate. Measures requiring two-thirds approval generally require 54 and 27 votes, respectively. A unified majority caucus can meet those thresholds without minority-party support.
 CRPA’s experience in 2026 shows that legislative advocacy can still produce important results under difficult circumstances.
 Throughout the last legislative session, CRPA’s Legislative Director, Rick Travis, maintained our dedicated, full-time legislative presence in Sacramento. His work included monitoring bills, communicating with legislative offices, participating in hearings, reviewing amendments, and coordinating with allied organizations and individual gun owners.
 CRPA played a leading role in efforts that helped stop or improve several firearms bills. Those results reflected persistent advocacy, cooperation with other organizations, and participation by members who contacted their elected representatives.
 The new legislative composition does not eliminate opportunities for scrutiny, amendment, negotiation, or opposition. It does mean that the governing majority has sufficient votes to advance legislation without opposition-party support when its members agree.
 CRPA will continue its legislative work while maintaining a separate constitutional litigation program to address restrictions that warrant judicial review.
 CRPA’s legislative representation, constitutional litigation, firearms education, and related programs depend on members and voluntary contributors. Contributions help sustain experienced staff, legal research, attorneys, and the other resources these activities require.
 Support CRPA’s Continuing Work 
 Thank you for your continued involvement with CRPA.
 C.D. “Chuck” Michel 
 President 
 California Rifle & Pistol Association 
 Stay tuned for Part 2: Bills CRPA Fought in 2026!
